body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{MB}}\) be completed to prove a joint asymptotic-linear expansion and functional central limit theorem for the estimated marked arm laws and censoring survival through \(\tau\), such that the unique-cut derivative and a mesh \(o(n^{-1/2})\) condition yield conditionally consistent simultaneous multiplier bands for every lower and upper TV-SACE and RM-SACE endpoint on \(\mathcal T\)?
body.justification: This is the first-class unresolved content: it turns sharp population surfaces into simultaneous frequentist statements while exposing the full-horizon censoring and grid-bias bottlenecks.
body.gap: Bluhmki et al. handle smooth multivariate Nelson--Aalen processes, and Fang--Santos, Firpo--Galvao--Parker, and Cho--Russell handle nonsmooth optimized maps after a primitive limit; no opened result supplies their required composition here.
body.consumer: It would deliver simultaneous coverage for the clinically interpreted curves in Comment et al. on regions where the active survivor deadline is stable.

obligation.what_is_open: A joint uniform asymptotic-linear expansion for a fully specified marked complete-path estimator with estimated administrative-censoring survival, plus conditional consistency of its increment-level multiplier process after applying all upper and lower endpoint maps.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle does not define the censoring-survival estimator, its filtration and influence function, the marked arm-law estimator, or the multiplier weights. The supplied assumptions alone therefore do not determine the stochastic process whose functional central limit theorem and conditional law must be proved. Unique cuts settle the population envelope derivative but do not supply this missing primitive statistical theorem.
obligation.attempted: Derived the active-cut envelope derivative, the quotient derivative including estimated covariate weights, the complementary-cut lower derivative, RM integration, and an order bound for deterministic grid bias. A generic empirical-process composition cannot complete the proof without first specifying and proving the joint marked product-limit or IPCW influence representation with estimated censoring through the horizon.
obligation.partial_result:
The population endpoint map has the following proved derivative at a unique upper deadline cut.  Write \(F_\epsilon=F+\epsilon H_\epsilon\), where \(H_\epsilon\to H\) uniformly, and let \(u_\epsilon\) minimize \(F_\epsilon\).  Compactness of the cut domain and uniqueness of \(u_x^\star\) imply \(u_\epsilon\to u_x^\star\): otherwise a convergent subsequence would have a distinct limit minimizing \(F\).  The two optimality inequalities
\[
 F_\epsilon(u_\epsilon)\le F_\epsilon(u_x^\star),
 \qquad F(u_x^\star)\le F(u_\epsilon)
\]
sandwich the difference quotient between \(H_\epsilon(u_\epsilon)+o(1)\) and \(H_\epsilon(u_x^\star)+o(1)\).  Both converge to \(H(u_x^\star)\).  Thus, for a primitive perturbation \(h=(h_{p_x},h_{s_x},h_{K_x},h_{b_x})\),
\[
 dA_x^U(r,t)[h]=h_{s_x}(t)-h_{s_x}(u_x^\star)+h_{K_x}(u_x^\star,[0,r]),
\]
with both perturbation terms at \(\infty\) set to zero.  If \(N=\sum_xp_x(A_x-b_x)\) and \(S=\sum_xp_xs_x\), then
\[
 d\theta[h]=\frac{dN[h]-\theta\,dS[h]}{S},
\]
where
\[
 dN[h]=\sum_x\{h_{p_x}(A_x-b_x)+p_x(dA_x[h]-h_{b_x})\},
 \qquad
 dS[h]=\sum_x\{h_{p_x}s_x+p_xh_{s_x}\}.
\]
The lower derivative follows by applying the same formula to the complementary mark set, and \(d\rho(a,t)[h]=-\int_0^a d\theta(r,t)[h]\,dr\).  Bounded finite-part densities give deterministic interpolation bias \(O(\delta_m)\), so \(\delta_m=o(n^{-1/2})\) makes that bias negligible.  What remains unproved is the joint uniform asymptotic-linear representation and conditionally valid multiplier approximation for a precisely defined estimated-censoring marked-path estimator.
